body: In case anyone else needs to sidestep this you can create a `app/manifest.webmanifest/route.ts` and add `manifest: new URL("manifest.webmanifest", basePath)` to your root `layout.tsx` metadata

I'm not absolutely sure, but it seems #53455 also suffers from a bug related to using a custom base path for metadata fields. I really feel that NextJS isn't tested enough with subdomains or subdirectories, which is a major regret.

Also, the `metadataBase` does not play well with `basePath` from `next.config.js`.

If you define `metadataBase` as `https://domain/with/path` and have `basePath` set to `/with/path`, then the resulting `og:image` has the URL `https://domain/with/path/with/path/opengraph-image.png`.

Ideally, there is no need to define `metadataBase` since it is already completely known with `basePath`. Otherwise, if `metadataBase` has a value, it should be used as an override.
I am wondering if perhaps this is related as well https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions/60787

body: I've found that the "manifest" field inside the metadata is completely ignored if there is a manifest file present in the app folder. As soon as the manifest file is removed it works correctly fetching from the provided url.

It seems that Next.js automatically adds the manifest link header, ignoring the basePath set in the next.config.js. The resulting tag generated is shown below. 

```<link rel="manifest" href="/manifest.webmanifest">```

body:
I ran into the same issue with the `manifest.ts` and  also `icon.png` files not being loaded properly. For me it's like this
- the `manifest.ts` file was not fetched with basePath prefix (`<link rel="manifest" href="/manifest.webmanifest">`)
- the icon's `href` does have `basePath` prefix (`<link rel="icon" href="/base-path/icon.png?....." />`) but I think the icon image was not being served properly, therefore the web's icon also didn't show up.

### Workaround

If your manifest/icon file is static file like mine, this workaround might help:

Try moving the files into the public folder like this:
```
project-root
├── public
│   ├── manifest.json
│   └── icon.png
├── app
│   ├── layout.tsx
│   └── page.tsx
└── ...
```

Then specify their path in layout file's `metadata` object.

```tsx
// app/layout.tsx

import type { Metadata } from 'next'

export const metadata: Metadata = {
  // ...
  manifest: `${BASE_PATH}/manifest.json`,
  icons: [
    {
      url: `${BASE_PATH}/icon.png`,
      sizes: '32x32',
      type: 'image/png',
    },
  ],
}
```

issue.title: fix metadata basePath for manifest
issue.body:
### What

Static metadata manifest file should be prefixed with `basePath` when it's specified, as all the requests are sent to the routes under `/<basePath>/*`, it should also show the correct url in the html

Fixes #56687
Closes NEXT-2707
